statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains low because the overnight range still contains price after a completed round trip, while stress is high across the energy, rates, yen and trade channels.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with a narrow flagged window from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC covering the post-holiday US cash reopen. Tail stays well below the block threshold; the elevated readings sit in stress rather than in a persistent no-retracement price path.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its overnight range as Brent near $99, revived rate-hike talk and fresh Canada tariffs lift stress into the US reopen
body: NQ futures trade near 29,578, up 0.04% on the session, and the day's range is still 29,478.00 to 29,764.75: the overnight advance was fully retraced earlier and the past hour added no extension in either direction. Price sits mid-range rather than near an extreme, and that intact retracement mechanism, with VIX at 15.70, is the central reason tail risk stays low; mean reversion is visibly still working rather than failing. Stress is a separate matter and has broadened again. WTI trades near $94.41 and Brent near $99.00, the highest since 24 July, after verified Houthi strikes on Saudi energy facilities that wounded 73 people and halted operations at some installations. The energy premium is compounded by reduced tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and by an Iranian threat to declare a maritime exclusion zone in the Persian Gulf. The rates channel remains live with the 2-year near 4.34% and the 10-year near 4.78%, and higher energy costs have revived talk of a Federal Reserve hike after August payrolls added 162,000. A third channel opened overnight: Canadian retaliatory tariffs of 15% to 50% on roughly $20 billion of US goods took effect at 04:01 UTC, though the exposure is concentrated in industrials, steel and consumer staples rather than in Nasdaq constituents. Cross-asset signals conflict rather than align: Nasdaq-100 futures are flat while Dow futures are down about 0.8%, S&P futures about 0.3% and Russell futures about 0.3%, and the latest session showed all seven tracked semiconductors higher against five of eight megacaps lower. Asia was weaker, with the Nikkei down 1.7% and the yen firm near 154 on intervention and Bank of Japan rate-hike speculation ahead of the 17-18 September meeting. US cash equities reopen at 13:30 UTC after the Labor Day holiday, which is the flagged window; that reopen is treated as a checkpoint, not as observed one-way structure.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed in the EA_ON band with tail between 5 and 10 and no reading near the block threshold. Stress climbed from the mid-50s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to just under 70 this morning as crude extended on the Saudi refinery strikes and the yen and trade channels opened up, while the dominant mode moved from normal to mixed as cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The near-term focus is the 13:30 UTC US cash reopen after the Labor Day holiday, where concentrated post-holiday order flow lifts conditional tail into the mid teens for the first two cash hours before easing through the midday lull, the 15:00 UTC NY Fed inflation expectations print and the 17:00 UTC 3-year auction. Overnight, two channels can produce a step change in either direction: Middle East energy headlines, which now carry both a supply-disruption strand and an Iranian maritime exclusion-zone threat, and Tokyo-hours yen strength into the 17-18 September Bank of Japan meeting. Beyond this horizon, PPI on 10 September, Oracle results the same week, CPI on 11 September and the 15-16 September FOMC meeting form the event stack; conditional tail is raised only modestly at the end of the horizon to reflect that build-up rather than any observed structure.
